model_annotations.Bulgarian: Диаграмата илюстрира сравнението на перплекситета за две модели – Per-Output и Per-Layer – при различни стойности на разредеността (Sparsity Rate), изразена в проценти. По хоризонталната ос са представени стойностите на разредеността: 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 60%, 70% и 80%, подредени във възходящ ред. Вертикалната ос представлява перплекситета, измерен в логаритмична скала, с диапазон от 1 до 1000, като се използват етикети 10⁰, 10¹ и 10², които съответстват на 1, 10 и 100. Диаграмата показва групирани стълбове за всеки ниво на разреденост, където синият стълб представлява Per-Output, а оранжевият – Per-Layer. Стойностите на перплекситета за двете модели се увеличават с увеличаване на разредеността, като за 80% разреденост и двете модели достигат най-високите стойности, приблизително 900 за Per-Output и 1000 за Per-Layer. Всеки стълб е визуализиран със съответния цвят, като легендата в горния ляв ъгъл разграничава двата модела.
model_annotations.Chinese: The bar chart compares the perplexity of two models, Per-Output and Per-Layer, across different sparsity rates ranging from 10% to 80%. The horizontal axis represents the sparsity rate, with categories labeled as 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 60%, 70%, and 80%, arranged in ascending order. The vertical axis, labeled "Perplexity," is plotted on a logarithmic scale, with values ranging from 10⁰ (1) to 10³ (1000), marked at intervals of 10⁰, 10¹, and 10². For each sparsity rate, two bars are displayed side-by-side: a blue bar for Per-Output and an orange bar for Per-Layer. The chart shows that for sparsity rates of 10% and 20%, both models have a perplexity value of approximately 1. As the sparsity rate increases, the perplexity for both models generally increases, with the Per-Layer model consistently showing a higher perplexity than the Per-Output model at each rate. At 80% sparsity, the Per-Output model has a perplexity of approximately 600, while the Per-Layer model has a perplexity of approximately 1000, making it the tallest bar in the chart. The shortest bars are the blue and orange bars at 10% and 20% sparsity, both at a height of 1. The bars are arranged in groups of two for each sparsity rate, with the Per-Output bar on the left and the Per-Layer bar on the right. There are no visual emphases such as shadows, bolding, or annotations on any of the bars.
model_annotations.English: The bar chart compares the perplexity of two models, Per-Output and Per-Layer, across varying sparsity rates from 10% to 80%. The x-axis represents the sparsity rate, with values of 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 60%, 70%, and 80%, while the y-axis shows perplexity on a logarithmic scale, ranging from 1 to 1000. For each sparsity rate, two bars are displayed: a blue bar for Per-Output and an orange bar for Per-Layer. At sparsity rates of 10% and 20%, both models have a perplexity of approximately 1. At 30%, the perplexity increases to about 1.5 for both models. At 40%, the perplexity is around 2.5 for both. At 50%, it rises to approximately 4.5 for both. At 60%, the perplexity is about 7.5 for both. At 70%, the perplexity increases to around 15 for Per-Output and 30 for Per-Layer. At 80%, the perplexity reaches approximately 500 for Per-Output and 1000 for Per-Layer. The chart shows that as sparsity increases, the perplexity for both models increases, with Per-Layer consistently having a higher perplexity than Per-Output at each sparsity rate.
model_annotations.German: Das Balkendiagramm zeigt den Zusammenhang zwischen der Sparsität (Sparsity Rate) und der Perplexität für zwei verschiedene Modelle oder Ansätze, bezeichnet als „Per-Output“ und „Per-Layer“. Die horizontale Achse stellt die Sparsität in Prozent dar, mit Werten von 10% bis 80% in 10%-Schritten. Die vertikale Achse stellt die Perplexität auf einer logarithmischen Skala dar, mit Beschriftungen bei 10⁻¹, 10⁰, 10¹ und 10². Für jede Sparsitätsrate sind zwei nebeneinander stehende Balken dargestellt: ein blauer Balken für „Per-Output“ und ein orangefarbener Balken für „Per-Layer“. Die Balken sind in der Reihenfolge der Sparsitätsraten angeordnet. Der höchste Balken ist der orangefarbene „Per-Layer“-Balken bei 80% Sparsität, der eine Perplexität von etwa 10³ erreicht. Der niedrigste Balken ist der blaue „Per-Output“-Balken bei 10% Sparsität, der eine Perplexität von etwa 10⁻¹ anzeigt. Die Legende oben links identifiziert die beiden Balkentypen.
